_comment: Sanitized samples of logo.dev Search Brands responses, shaped exactly like the
documented array-of-brand-objects body the DAT-010 client parses.
Every domain is under a reserved .example TLD and every company name is
invented. Nothing here is a real brand, a real customer, or a real prospect,
and no API key, quota, or account identifier appears anywhere: these are
SHAPES the policy must handle, captured so the practical v1 rules are proved
against realistic provider output rather than against hand-written dicts that
only ever contain what the policy expects.
The awkward shapes are the point. A brand search asked for a company name it
does not know answers with whatever it does know — a LinkedIn page, a
directory listing, a website builder, a domain for sale — and the policy has
to reject all of those without ever leaving the capture looking resolved.

clean_single_match._note: One brand whose name and domain both match the query. Resolves to provisional — never confirmed, because one provider agreeing with itself is not corroboration.

two_plausible_matches_for_this_capture._note: The same ambiguity, for the employer the committed capture fixture names. Kept separate so the web tests can reach the conflicting-candidates state through the real capture rather than by editing one.

two_plausible_matches._note: Two brands that both align with the query. Stays unresolved: choosing between equally-matching companies is exactly the guess this policy exists to avoid.

platforms_and_directories._note: The realistic failure mode: the provider answers with the places a company appears rather than the company. Every entry is rejected with its own reason and the capture stays unresolved.

unrelated_top_rank._note: The provider's first result is confidently wrong. Rank is recorded and ignored; no candidate aligns, so nothing is selected.

malformed_entry._note: A brand object carrying an unusable domain. It is rejected as invalid rather than normalized into something that looks plausible.

empty._note: Searched, and the provider genuinely has nothing. Truthfully unresolved, and distinct from a provider that could not be reached.
